wrong: For assigning punishment levels

For grouping by home province

Visiting schedules are set by facility rules, not by classification.
Unit for the most dangerous inmates in prison
That is the maximum security compound.
Hospital ward that treats sick or injured inmates
That is the prison hospital, not the reception and diagnostic center.
Area where inmates receive family visitors
That is the visiting area.
Revenge for the victim's family
Modern corrections rejects revenge as a purpose of imprisonment.
Cheap labor for the state
Inmate work is part of rehabilitation, not the purpose of imprisonment.
Public shaming of offenders
Shaming is not a purpose of imprisonment.
Bureau of Jail Management and Penology (BJMP)
BJMP manages city, district and municipal jails, not national prisons.
Parole and Probation Administration (PPA)
The PPA supervises probationers and parolees in the community.
Philippine National Police (PNP)
The PNP holds arrested persons only briefly; it does not run national prisons.
Bureau of Jail Management and Parole
The P stands for Penology; parole is handled by the Board of Pardons and Parole.
Bureau of Justice Management and Penology
The J stands for Jail, not Justice.
Board of Jail Management and Protection

Jail for women, prison for men
Both jails and prisons hold men and women; the difference is the length of the sentence.
Jail is run by courts, prison by police
Jails are run by BJMP and prisons by BuCor; neither is run by courts or police.
They are the same facility
Jails and prisons differ in who runs them and the length of sentences they hold.
Provincial jail in Bulacan
New Bilibid Prison is a national penitentiary, not a provincial jail.
City jail in Quezon City
City jails are run by BJMP; New Bilibid Prison is run by BuCor.
Juvenile facility in Muntinlupa for minors
Children in conflict with the law go to a Bahay Pag-asa, not to New Bilibid Prison.
Inmates who are the most dangerous
They go to maximum security.
First-time offenders only, of any risk
Security level depends on risk, not on being a first offender.
Detainees still awaiting their trial in court
Detainees awaiting trial are held in jails, not in prison security levels.
Most dangerous inmates
They go to maximum security.
Inmates with high escape risk
High escape risk calls for maximum or medium security.
Inmates serving life terms
Inmates serving life terms are maximum security.
Station where suspects are booked
That is a police station.
Building where trials are held
That is a courthouse.
Hospital for sick inmates
That is a prison hospital, not the prison itself.
Agency managing city and municipal jails
That is the BJMP.
Agency supervising probationers and parolees
That is the Parole and Probation Administration.
Agency prosecuting criminal cases
Prosecution is done by the DOJ's prosecutors, not BuCor.
Punishment of inmates
Punishment is part of a sentence, but BuCor's main goal is safekeeping and rehabilitation.
Earning revenue
BuCor is not a business; its goal is to rehabilitate inmates.
Isolation of offenders
Isolation alone is not the goal; inmates are prepared to return to society.
Undersecretary of Justice
The DOJ supervises BuCor, but BuCor itself is headed by a Director General.
Commissioner of Corrections
There is no such post; BuCor is headed by a Director General.
Chief Jail Warden
A warden heads a single jail; BuCor is headed by a Director General.
Maximum security prison in the city
A penal colony is an open, agricultural facility, usually far from cities.
Detention center for persons awaiting trial
Persons awaiting trial are held in jails.
Island facility for juvenile offenders
Children are not sent to penal colonies; they go to a Bahay Pag-asa.

Housing inmates together in a dormitory
